newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-SORENSTAM CONFIDENT AS SHE EYES RECORD U.S. OPEN HAT-TRICK.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SORENSTAM CONFIDENT AS SHE EYES RECORD U.S. OPEN HAT-TRICK.

text.p: Annika Sorenstam has no complaints about her game as she prepares an assault on an unprecedented third straight U.S. Women's Open title starting Thursday at Pumpkin Ridge.
"I'm so consistent nowadays," said the 26-year-old Swede.
"The way I started this year was incredible. I still can't believe it," she added. "It's given me a lot of confidence."
Sorenstam has already won four times in 13 starts on the LPGA Tour this year, and leads the money list with $779,862.

Sorenstam is favoured these days everywhere she plays, but particularly at the U.S. Open, where par is valued. She is not the longest, nor the most aggressive player, but usually makes the fewest mistakes, which is what generally wins U.S. Opens.
Of the five previous women to have won two consecutive titles, Donna Caponi came closest to completing a hat-trick, finishing tied for third in 1971.
Sorenstam had her first practice round Tuesday on the Pumpkin Ridge course, which last year hosted the U.S. Amateur championship won by Tiger Woods.

"It's probably one of the best courses I've ever played," Sorenstam said. "I can't remember a bad hole. There's a lot of planning around this course. I like it when the greens are small. You've got to place your ball.
"My strength is my irons right now, I'm hitting my seven, eight and nine iron really well. Hopefully my rhythm and swing will be there this week."
Sorenstam took last week off to relax and practice, and spend time with her parents, who are here to watch her play.
"I needed a week off to get ready. I did play a little golf, but I didn't overdo it."
Despite winning the U.S. Open last year, Sorenstam surrendered the money title to Australian Karrie Webb.
Their rivalry is considered the best thing going for women's golf, and Sorenstam is the first to admit that she was inspired by Webb's success.

"The way Karrie played made me want to work hard," Sorenstam continued. "I wanted to win the money list again and that was my goal this year. I've worked hard on my weaknesses, which have been my short game and putting."
Webb and Sorenstam will be able to keep a good eye on each other, because they will play the first two rounds together.
Webb, currently second on this year's money list, is probably the woman most likely to prevent Sorenstam from creating history this week.

"I like this course because I think it eliminates a few players," Webb said. "You can't bounce it onto the green and there are a lot of water carries. I'm a high-ball hitter, so I think that's one of the advantages I have."
Webb has no doubt Sorenstam is the woman to beat.

"She definitely is a U.S. Open player. She doesn't make too many mistakes and she has the mental game for a U.S. Open too. She is very patient and that's something I'm going to concentrate on this week."
Another player to watch, if she can solve the putting problems that have dogged her recently, is Britain's Laura Davies, the 1987 champion.
The most probable American contenders include Kelly Robbins, Nancy Lopez, Tammie Green and Michelle McGann.
Robbins last Sunday set the LPGA Tour's all-time low scoring record as she won the Jamie Farr Kroger Classic at 19-under-par 265.
